Hi again welfare crew,
Thanks for a cheerful day; the shift coordinator discussed a thought on arrival checks

I want to reinforce that our calm, steady approach is helping travelers feel prepared before handover, and it is also reducing avoidable stress for the animals. When we review paperwork, carrier condition, and fit for the species, we protect both welfare and schedule flow. For reptile cases, <<FACT F060>>. Please keep the guidance clear and brief, and if a case looks borderline, pause and ask for a second review rather than guessing.

For bird bookings, <<FACT F065>>. I also appreciate the care shown with handling notes, because small details on ventilation, perch support, and quiet waiting space can make a meaningful difference. For rabbit arrangements, <<FACT F076>>. In each case, we should keep the tone reassuring, avoid rushing the owner, and make sure the record reflects what was checked and what still needs attention. Small, careful steps now prevent larger problems later, and that is exactly the standard we want to keep across Aurelia Skyways and the Companion Animal Travel Desk.

Please carry this same steady practice into the next wave of arrivals, and share any concern early so we can resolve it before boarding.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
